messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for Wireless Communication without making unsupported claims?

已查到可引用的部分資料：

## Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor without unsupported claims, the comparison needs formal R&S specifications / features / ordering evidence for our products, official competitor specifications or third-party evidence for competitor claims, and matched test conditions, versions, option stacks, limits, and validation reports for every technical or commercial claim being compared [6][21][53][73].
## Required evidence checklist
| Claim type | Evidence required before comparing | Why required |
|---|---|---|
| Our signaling tester capability | Use CMX500 formal specifications and Features and Functions, including document ID, version, date / software version, option codes, order numbers, and stated limits [73][74][75]. | The CMX500 page separates binding specifications from Features and Functions, and states that non-traceable specs, typical data, nominal values, measured values, and data without tolerance limits are not guaranteed / not binding [73]. |
| Our non-signaling / production tester capability | Use CMP180 Specifications Version 08.00 and CMP180 Features and Functions Version 09, including software version, document identifiers, option codes, RF generator/analyzer configuration, measurement ranges, and tolerance limits [21][49][51][53]. | CMP180 Features and Functions is only a test applications overview, and measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be checked in specifications document PD 3609.7348.22 [53]. |
| Competitor technical capability | Use the competitor’s official datasheets, specifications, configuration guides, order numbers, document versions, release dates, and supported configuration details [6][36][38]. | Current Keysight and Anritsu comparison pages are based mainly on R&S internal sales battle cards and cannot replace official competitor specifications [4][6][34][36]. |
| Direct R&S-vs-competitor claims | Use evidence that directly compares the same feature under the same scope, not separate R&S and competitor facts placed side by side [5][35]. | The existing CMX500 vs Keysight and CMX500 vs Anritsu tables are sales positioning, and their own limitations say the claims require formal R&S option checks and competitor official evidence [5][35]. |
| Frequency, bandwidth, throughput, MIMO, carrier aggregation, or RF claims | Provide exact hardware, software, band combination, carrier count, SCS, modulation, MIMO layers, bandwidth, calibration conditions, and binding tolerance limits [25][70][73]. | Existing battle-card claims such as FR1 up to 18 GHz, RFU18 aggregated NR bandwidth 2000 MHz, and FR3 claims are flagged as sales / roadmap wording and not binding specifications without formal documents and test conditions [25][40][70]. |
| WLAN signaling / measurement comparison | For CMX500, cite WLAN signaling and measurement options such as CMX-KS350B / KS351B / KS352B / KS355B / KS356B / KS360B and CMX-KM350 / KM351 / KM352 / KM360, and for the competitor cite the competitor’s official WLAN support evidence [48][62]. | CMX500 WLAN options are supported in the Features and Functions / configuration passages, while competitor WLAN statements in battle cards require official competitor evidence [6][36][48][62]. |
| Application, IP, automation, fading, or protocol workflow comparison | Provide exact option codes, software versions, workflows, external-tool requirements, and supported measurements for both sides [6][71][72]. | The CMX500 evidence lists GUI, scripting, IP application, IMS, throughput, and analysis functions, while competitor workflow claims such as RaySim / Atlas / Channel Studio still need official functional boundaries and versions [6][71][72]. |
| Conformance, certification, “validated,” or operator-acceptance claims | Provide validation report, test case list, PTCRB / GCF version, dates, and validation criteria [25][59]. | Existing sources explicitly say claims such as first validated NR-NTN conformance lack validation reports, PTCRB RFT 555 version, test case lists, or official validation datasets [25][59]. |
| De-sense or multi-technology interference comparison | Provide test cases, interference model, pass/fail limits, setup diagram, synchronization, shielding/chamber conditions, and automation flow [2][3]. | The UAV / De-sense source only provides a concept and configuration principle and does not provide test cases, limits, setup, shielding/chamber conditions, or automation flow [2][3]. |
| TCO, fewer boxes, “only platform,” “leadership,” or “best” claims | Provide a quantified TCO model, complete bill of materials, pricing / configuration basis, integration assumptions, and independent or official evidence for both sides [6][36][67]. | The passages identify “only platform,” “first,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” and “fewer boxes” as sales language, and the Keysight comparison notes that TCO lacks a formula or empirical evidence [6][36][67]. |
| Customer-facing configuration or quotation | Use formal configuration guides, product brochures, ordering data, release notes, pricing / configurator output, and local R&S confirmation where required [2][47][57]. | The UAV signaling configuration note is not final quotation or complete configuration, CMX500 Features and Functions is not a specifications datasheet, and GPRF / roadmap claims require release notes or formal documentation [2][47][57]. |
## Current evidence limitation
The available competitor comparison pages can support that R&S battle cards position CMX500 against Keysight or Anritsu, but those pages themselves state that the material is sales positioning, not binding technical specifications, and that official competitor evidence is still needed for customer-facing claims [4][6][34][36].
【推論】A defensible Wireless Communication comparison should therefore be built as a claim-by-claim evidence matrix: CMX500 signaling claims from CMX500 specifications / features, CMP180 non-signaling claims from CMP180 specifications / features, and every competitor claim from official competitor documents or independent evidence with matching test conditions [21][53][73][74][75].

Signaling test solution › 重點摘要
- 本來源是 OneNote 複製出的 [[UAV]] signaling test solution 筆記，raw 轉檔日期為 2026-09-17；正文未標示正式發布日期、作者、文件版次或適用客戶 / 專案。
- 來源指出無人機常使用多種通信技術，例子包含 proprietary radio / image transmission、Wi‑Fi、[[LTE]]、未來 [[5G]]、[[RTK]]、[[SATCOM]] 與 encrypted frequency-hopping radio。
- 來源以多款無人機 / UAV 產品為例整理核心通訊技術：[[DJI Mini 4 Pro]]、[[DJI Mavic 3]]、[[DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise]]、[[Parrot ANAFI Ai]]、[[XAG P100]]、[[Skydio X2E]]、[[RQ-4 Global Hawk]] 與 [[Switchblade]]。
- 來源稱 [[R&S CMX500]] RF frequency range 為 **400 MHz 至 8 GHz**，可提供 [[LTE]]、[[5G]] 與 [[Wi-Fi]] UE 的單一技術 signaling test。
- 來源列出 signaling test 可包含基本 RF 量測、application layer tests 與 protocol test；基本 RF 量測項目包含 Power、Frequency、Spectrum、[[EVM]]、[[PER]] / [[BLER]]、[[MIMO]]。
- 來源列出一組 [[R&S CMX500]] 5G test configuration，包含 [[R&S CMX-PB70H]]、[[R&S CMX-B200A]]、[[R&S CMX-B300C]]、[[R&S CMX-B600B]]、[[R&S CMX-KA100]] 與 [[R&S CMX-KM600]]。
- 來源列出一組 [[R&S CMX500]] Wi‑Fi test configuration，包含 WLAN signaling、WLAN TX measurement 與 WLAN ARB generator options，例如 [[R&S CMX-KS350B]]、[[R&S CMX-KS351B]]、[[R&S CMX-KS352B]]、[[R&S CMX-KS355B]]、[[R&S CMX-KS356B]]、[[R&S CMX-KS360B]]、[[R&S CMX-KM350]]、[[R&S CMX-KM351]]、[[R&S CMX-KM352]]、[[R&S CMX-KM360]]、[[R&S CMX-KW350]]、[[R&S CMX-KW351]]、[[R&S CMX-KW352]]。
- 來源指出如果 UAV 使用兩種以上通訊技術，通訊技術之間可能造成相互干擾；基於 [[R&S CMX500]] 支援多種通訊技術，可進行 De-sense validation。
- 來源對多技術整合驗證的配置原則是：software options 合併上述 5G 與 Wi‑Fi 表格，hardware 以滿足兩者中最大的 carrier aggregation 或 [[MIMO]] 作為配置。
- 來源末尾列出兩個待讀材料：本機 PDF `5G-hardening-against-smart-jammer-attacks_wp_en_3610-1591-52_v0100.pdf`，以及 SharePoint 上 `Making Deployed 5G Private Networks more Resilient.pptx`；正文未擷取。

## Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor without unsupported claims, the comparison needs formal R&S specifications / features / ordering evidence for our products, official competitor specifications or third-party evidence for competitor claims, and matched test conditions, versions, option stacks, limits, and validation reports for every technical or commercial claim being compared [6][21][53][73].
## Required evidence checklist
| Claim type | Evidence required before comparing | Why required |
|---|---|---|
| Our signaling tester capability | Use CMX500 formal specifications and Features and Functions, including document ID, version, date / software version, option codes, order numbers, and stated limits [73][74][75]. | The CMX500 page separates binding specifications from Features and Functions, and states that non-traceable specs, typical data, nominal values, measured values, and data without tolerance limits are not guaranteed / not binding [73]. |
| Our non-signaling / production tester capability | Use CMP180 Specifications Version 08.00 and CMP180 Features and Functions Version 09, including software version, document identifiers, option codes, RF generator/analyzer configuration, measurement ranges, and tolerance limits [21][49][51][53]. | CMP180 Features and Functions is only a test applications overview, and measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be checked in specifications document PD 3609.7348.22 [53]. |
| Competitor technical capability | Use the competitor’s official datasheets, specifications, configuration guides, order numbers, document versions, release dates, and supported configuration details [6][36][38]. | Current Keysight and Anritsu comparison pages are based mainly on R&S internal sales battle cards and cannot replace official competitor specifications [4][6][34][36]. |
| Direct R&S-vs-competitor claims | Use evidence that directly compares the same feature under the same scope, not separate R&S and competitor facts placed side by side [5][35]. | The existing CMX500 vs Keysight and CMX500 vs Anritsu tables are sales positioning, and their own limitations say the claims require formal R&S option checks and competitor official evidence [5][35]. |
| Frequency, bandwidth, throughput, MIMO, carrier aggregation, or RF claims | Provide exact hardware, software, band combination, carrier count, SCS, modulation, MIMO layers, bandwidth, calibration conditions, and binding tolerance limits [25][70][73]. | Existing battle-card claims such as FR1 up to 18 GHz, RFU18 aggregated NR bandwidth 2000 MHz, and FR3 claims are flagged as sales / roadmap wording and not binding specifications without formal documents and test conditions [25][40][70]. |
| WLAN signaling / measurement comparison | For CMX500, cite WLAN signaling and measurement options such as CMX-KS350B / KS351B / KS352B / KS355B / KS356B / KS360B and CMX-KM350 / KM351 / KM352 / KM360, and for the competitor cite the competitor’s official WLAN support evidence [48][62]. | CMX500 WLAN options are supported in the Features and Functions / configuration passages, while competitor WLAN statements in battle cards require official competitor evidence [6][36][48][62]. |
| Application, IP, automation, fading, or protocol workflow comparison | Provide exact option codes, software versions, workflows, external-tool requirements, and supported measurements for both sides [6][71][72]. | The CMX500 evidence lists GUI, scripting, IP application, IMS, throughput, and analysis functions, while competitor workflow claims such as RaySim / Atlas / Channel Studio still need official functional boundaries and versions [6][71][72]. |
| Conformance, certification, “validated,” or operator-acceptance claims | Provide validation report, test case list, PTCRB / GCF version, dates, and validation criteria [25][59]. | Existing sources explicitly say claims such as first validated NR-NTN conformance lack validation reports, PTCRB RFT 555 version, test case lists, or official validation datasets [25][59]. |
| De-sense or multi-technology interference comparison | Provide test cases, interference model, pass/fail limits, setup diagram, synchronization, shielding/chamber conditions, and automation flow [2][3]. | The UAV / De-sense source only provides a concept and configuration principle and does not provide test cases, limits, setup, shielding/chamber conditions, or automation flow [2][3]. |
| TCO, fewer boxes, “only platform,” “leadership,” or “best” claims | Provide a quantified TCO model, complete bill of materials, pricing / configuration basis, integration assumptions, and independent or official evidence for both sides [6][36][67]. | The passages identify “only platform,” “first,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” and “fewer boxes” as sales language, and the Keysight comparison notes that TCO lacks a formula or empirical evidence [6][36][67]. |
| Customer-facing configuration or quotation | Use formal configuration guides, product brochures, ordering data, release notes, pricing / configurator output, and local R&S confirmation where required [2][47][57]. | The UAV signaling configuration note is not final quotation or complete configuration, CMX500 Features and Functions is not a specifications datasheet, and GPRF / roadmap claims require release notes or formal documentation [2][47][57]. |
## Current evidence limitation
